tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.summary: What Genesys Cloud CX is, where an organization lives, and how a voice conversation is supposed to move.

lessons.title: What Genesys Cloud CX is
lessons.summary: Genesys Cloud CX is a subscription contact-center platform with four nested packages, not a single feature switch.

lessons.title: Core regions and satellite media
lessons.summary: An organization is born in one core AWS region. Satellite regions carry media. They do not host the org.

lessons.title: SIP, RTP, and what the trunk is doing
lessons.summary: SIP sets the call up. RTP moves the audio. They are different protocols, and Genesys trunks speak both.

lessons.title: What ACD is before you name a queue
lessons.summary: ACD picks an agent for a waiting interaction. The queue is the waiting line. Skills, utilization, and On Queue decide who is eligible.

lessons.title: Digital conversations beside voice
lessons.summary: Voice is one media. Architect also has inbound message, email, and chat flows, and queues track those medias separately.

lessons.title: Divisions, before roles get complicated
lessons.summary: A division groups objects inside one organization. It is not a second org, and the Home division cannot be deleted.

lessons.title: How to read a Genesys page without inventing the rest
lessons.summary: This lab cites the Resource Center, the Developer Center, Genesys Education, and RFCs. The page wins when they differ.

lessons.title: Prerequisites before the first trunk
lessons.summary: BYOC Cloud needs a public carrier address, an open port plan, and a real location. The org subscription has to include the telephony product you intend to use.

tracks.title: Organization and licensing
tracks.summary: Regions, roles, divisions, named and concurrent licenses, packages, and fair use.

lessons.title: Place the organization in a core region
lessons.summary: You do not move an org between regions as a setting. You create it in a core region and live with that login host.

lessons.title: Roles are permission lists paired with divisions
lessons.summary: A role without a division grant does not open objects. An OAuth client inherits only a subset of its creator’s pairs.

lessons.title: Named licenses and the concurrent peak
lessons.summary: Concurrent billing charges the peak of simultaneous users, and it ignores peaks shorter than 30 minutes.

lessons.title: Pick CX 1, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4 on purpose
lessons.summary: Match the package to the job. Do not buy CX 1 and then design a WFM project.

lessons.title: People, queues, and the 5,000 member line
lessons.summary: Users live in the org. Queue membership is not the same thing as a division, and it has a hard cap.

lessons.title: Fair use is a pool, not a mystery invoice
lessons.summary: Licenses include monthly allowances. Overage is priced on the policy page. Copying the numbers into a design doc freezes them wrong.

lessons.title: A first-week admin checklist
lessons.summary: Week one is region, divisions, roles, packages, one queue, and a published in-queue flow. Telephony can follow.

tracks.title: Architect flows
tracks.summary: Flow types, tasks, in-queue experiences, data actions, bots, secure calls, and publish.

lessons.title: The flow types on the Architect home page
lessons.summary: Architect is a list of flow types. Picking the wrong tab is the first defect.

lessons.title: Tasks, menus, and a way out
lessons.summary: An inbound call flow plays audio, collects input, and must transfer, hand off, or disconnect.

lessons.title: In-queue flows are the hold experience
lessons.summary: The caller is already queued. The in-queue flow is what they hear or read while ACD looks for an agent.

lessons.title: Data actions and participant data
lessons.summary: A data action calls a system outside the flow. Participant data carries a value to the agent.

lessons.title: Common modules are how you stop copying tasks
lessons.summary: A common module is a flow type you call from other flows. The name is still unique inside that type.

lessons.title: Secure call flows keep digits away from the recording
lessons.summary: A secure flow is how a caller enters a card number without that audio being recorded or shown to the agent.

lessons.title: Call a bot from the inbound flow
lessons.summary: Dialog Engine bot flows and digital bot flows are Architect flow types. The inbound flow calls them. It does not become them.

lessons.title: Publish, division, and Flow Insights
lessons.summary: A saved flow is a draft. The runtime uses the published version. Insights tell you whether anyone hit it.

tracks.title: ACD routing
tracks.summary: Standard, bullseye, preferred, predictive, and conditional routing, plus the two scoring methods.

lessons.title: Five routing methods
lessons.summary: Standard, predictive, bullseye, preferred agent, and conditional group routing are the methods on a queue.

lessons.title: All skills, best available, or disregard
lessons.summary: The evaluation method is how standard and bullseye decide that an agent “has the skills.”

lessons.title: Conversation score and priority score
lessons.summary: One priority point on conversation score is worth 60,000 milliseconds of arrival time.

lessons.title: Bullseye rings widen the target
lessons.summary: Up to five rings. A delay from 2 seconds to 72 hours. Up to 50 skills removed on a ring.

lessons.title: Preferred agents are tried first
lessons.summary: A preferred agent is considered even without the required skills, and only if they are a member of the queue and On Queue.

lessons.title: Predictive routing is a KPI model with a timeout
lessons.summary: Predictive routing can run for everyone, in a comparison test, or at a fixed 80/20 split you cannot edit.

lessons.title: Conditional group routing borrows agents carefully
lessons.summary: A rule is a KPI plus agent availability. The other queue must be able to spare the people.

lessons.title: Utilization and Not Responding
lessons.summary: A fully utilized agent is skipped. An agent who ignores an alert becomes Not Responding.

tracks.title: Queues, skills, and wrap-up
tracks.summary: Queue media settings, skills, wrap-up codes, callbacks, and service level.

lessons.title: Create the queue in a division
lessons.summary: The queue is a named waiting line in one division, with at most 5,000 members.

lessons.title: Skills and proficiency are on the agent
lessons.summary: The queue asks for skills. The agent profile holds them. Evaluation decides whether proficiency matters.

lessons.title: After call work and the system wrap-up codes
lessons.summary: ACW is optional, discretionary, or time-boxed. The platform has its own codes when agents do not finish.

lessons.title: Wrap-up codes live in divisions too
lessons.summary: The codes an agent sees are the codes their role can see, and Genesys wants them in the queue’s division.

lessons.title: Service level is a percentage and a target in seconds
lessons.summary: Each media has a service level percentage and a target duration. That pair is what conditional routing and WFM both mean by “the goal.”

lessons.title: Callbacks are interactions with their own rules
lessons.summary: A callback is queued work. It still needs a wrap-up code, and it counts as its own utilization slot.

lessons.title: Membership, On Queue, and the copy trap
lessons.summary: A copied queue can duplicate a bullseye you did not mean to clone.

tracks.title: BYOC Cloud and SIP trunks
tracks.summary: Carrier and PBX trunks, RTP over the internet, Dynamic Cloud Voice, and the quick-start order.

lessons.title: BYOC Cloud is your carrier, Genesys’ media
lessons.summary: You bring the carrier contract. Genesys terminates a SIP trunk on the AWS media tier. Audio is RTP on the internet.

lessons.title: Carrier trunks and PBX trunks
lessons.summary: BYOC Carrier and BYOC PBX are the two types. Carrier has subtypes. PBX has one.

lessons.title: The quick-start order
lessons.summary: Location, trunk, outbound route, number plan. The product on the subscription comes before all of that.

lessons.title: Dynamic Cloud Voice is the current platform
lessons.summary: New trunks start there. Moving an old trunk means allow lists, Amazon root CAs, TLS ciphers, and a toggle.

lessons.title: Number plans classify what people dial
lessons.summary: A site can hold 200 plans. DIDs do not need one for basic routing. Emergency, extension, and 988 already exist as defaults.

lessons.title: Watch the trunk, not only the flow
lessons.summary: When audio fails and Architect Insights still shows runs, the trunk is the next object.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud Voice is the other door
lessons.summary: If Genesys is the carrier, you buy numbers in a region that offers voice, and emergency is part of that product story rather than your trunk.

tracks.title: The Edge and BYOC Premises
tracks.summary: Premises Edges, Edge groups, phone trunks, sites, and what happens when the local Edge is down.

lessons.title: The premises Edge is the local media hop
lessons.summary: BYOC Premises puts an Edge on your network. Phones and trunks registered there do not need a public address the way BYOC Cloud does.

lessons.title: Local site routing stays home until it cannot
lessons.summary: Genesys uses Edges in the same site when it can. Another site is the exception.

lessons.title: Phone trunks, WebRTC, and inherit
lessons.summary: WebRTC and SIP phones are phone trunks on the Edge group. Inherit is the default you should verify.

lessons.title: When the local Edge is offline
lessons.summary: The documented failover is another site, if that site actually has the resource.

lessons.title: Choose Cloud, Premises, or both
lessons.summary: Use premises when the phones and the carrier are on your network. Use cloud when they are not. Use both only where each number has an owner.

lessons.title: A browser phone is still a network endpoint
lessons.summary: WebRTC removes the desk set. It does not remove media engineering.

lessons.title: Premises turn-up checklist
lessons.summary: Group, inherit, site, trunk, failover test, emergency owner.

tracks.title: Numbers and emergency calling
tracks.summary: E.164, emergency classifications, BYOC warnings, and Genesys Cloud Voice coverage.

lessons.title: Name the emergency owner before the DID
lessons.summary: Genesys is not responsible for emergency calls that ride a BYOC trunk. That sentence belongs in the design, not in the postmortem.

lessons.title: Emergency is a classification and a route
lessons.summary: The default Emergency plan matches 911 and 933 in the US and Canada, and 142 in Switzerland. It still needs a route.

lessons.title: The location is a physical place
lessons.summary: The quick start adds a location because services, including emergency, need a real site.

lessons.title: Voice coverage is a table, not a promise
lessons.summary: Country rows decide DID, toll-free, domestic, and international. FedRAMP and the sovereign region add harder edges.

lessons.title: Normalize toward E.164 on purpose
lessons.summary: Intra-country and inter-country plans normalize. Digit-length extensions and E.164 lists do not.

lessons.title: Test emergency like a change, not like a demo
lessons.summary: A live emergency test is a carrier and public-safety conversation. The call simulator is the part you can do alone.

tracks.title: Workforce management
tracks.summary: Business units, management units, service goals, schedules, adherence, and time off. WFM is a CX 3 capability.

lessons.title: WEM is a set of products, and WFM is one of them
lessons.summary: Recording, screen recording, quality, performance, speech and text analytics, and workforce management are the WEM list.

lessons.title: Business units and management units
lessons.summary: A business unit is the planning container. A management unit is the group of agents you actually schedule.

lessons.title: Service goal templates are the planning target
lessons.summary: The queue’s service level and the WFM template should describe the same promise.

lessons.title: Schedules are the plan agents work
lessons.summary: A schedule is built from the management unit, the goals, and activity codes. It is not a routing method.

lessons.title: Intraday and adherence compare the plan to the floor
lessons.summary: Adherence is the gap between the activity you scheduled and the status the agent is actually in.

lessons.title: Time off is a schedule change with a rule
lessons.summary: Time-off requests are part of WFM. An approved request that nobody reflects on the schedule is a rumor.

lessons.title: The workforce certification is a named exam
lessons.summary: The catalog lists a Workforce Management specialist certification and a preparation course. It does not list a code this lab is willing to invent.

tracks.title: Quality and recording
tracks.summary: Evaluation forms, calibration, coaching, recording policies, and the prerequisites for AI scoring.

lessons.title: Quality management evaluates the conversation
lessons.summary: QM records and scores interactions, and it can coach. It is not the schedule.

lessons.title: Forms have questions and weights
lessons.summary: The form is the rubric. Weights decide which questions move the score.

lessons.title: Recording policies choose calls and retention
lessons.summary: A policy decides which ACD calls are recorded and how long they are kept. A secure flow is a hole in a segment, not a substitute for the policy.

lessons.title: Coaching and disputes close the loop
lessons.summary: A score that the agent cannot see and cannot dispute is not a quality program.

lessons.title: AI scoring needs STA, QM, and tokens
lessons.summary: The FAQ is blunt: AI scoring requires Speech and Text Analytics, Quality Management, and AI Experience Tokens.

lessons.title: Retention, export, and the reason you recorded
lessons.summary: Export and AWS recording paths exist so a recording can leave the platform under a policy, not as a side copy.

tracks.title: Speech and text analytics
tracks.summary: What gets transcribed, how sentiment and topics are used, and why analysis is not the same thing as the live conversation.

lessons.title: STA reads the conversation after the channel has it
lessons.summary: Speech and text analytics covers voice and digital interactions. It is not a second ACD.

lessons.title: Sentiment is a label on the text, not a mood you can argue with
lessons.summary: Sentiment scores the customer’s language. Use it as a filter, then listen.

lessons.title: Topics, programs, and phrases are the dictionary
lessons.summary: A program groups topics. A topic is phrases you expect to hear or read.

lessons.title: Agent empathy is a detected behavior, still a form question
lessons.summary: Empathy detection points at calls. Calibration still decides what empathy means for your company.

lessons.title: Content search is how you test the dictionary
lessons.summary: Search the transcript before you trust a topic count.

lessons.title: Full analysis and a faster transcript are different clocks
lessons.summary: Some views wait until the interaction is complete. A lower-latency transcript path is a different API.

tracks.title: Genesys AI and bots
tracks.summary: Dialog Engine and digital bots, failure paths, Agent Copilot, tokens, and the AI exams as the catalog names them.

lessons.title: Two Architect bot types, plus Copilot beside the agent
lessons.summary: A bot flow talks to the customer. Agent Copilot talks to the agent. They are different products on different pages.

lessons.title: Dialog Engine bot flows are voice and digital intents
lessons.summary: You build the bot in Architect, then the inbound flow calls it.

lessons.title: Digital bot flows are a different call
lessons.summary: Message experiences use Digital Bot Flows and Call Digital Bot Flow.

lessons.title: Every bot has a failure output to a queue
lessons.summary: No-match, timeout, and error are normal. The queue is the design.

lessons.title: Agent Copilot assists the person who stayed on the interaction
lessons.summary: Knowledge, transcripts, scripts, next best action, and notes. The benefit is described as surviving a blind transfer.

lessons.title: Tokens are a published allotment, and a FAQ ratio you re-read
lessons.summary: The overview publishes CX 4 token counts. The STA FAQ publishes how AI scoring spends them.

lessons.title: The AI exams are named on the catalog, one exam each
lessons.summary: Two AI certifications. No invented exam codes.

tracks.title: Platform APIs
tracks.summary: OAuth grants, client credentials limits, region hosts, and why this lab’s explorer never sends a request.

lessons.title: The Developer Center is the map. This lab is not a client.
lessons.summary: Read the public docs. Do not point a tutorial at a production org.

lessons.title: Pick the grant that matches who the call runs as
lessons.summary: Client credentials, authorization code with PKCE, and SAML2 Bearer are the grants to learn. Implicit is the one leaving.

lessons.title: Client credentials have no user, so users/me is the wrong call
lessons.summary: The token is the client. The guide shows that limit on purpose.

lessons.title: Implicit grant is a migration, not a new design
lessons.summary: The OAuth article dates the deprecation: after 25 May 2026.

lessons.title: Login host and API host are a pair you look up
lessons.summary: US East is the pair this lab will quote in full. Other rows stay on the regions article.

lessons.title: Role and division pairs are the real permission
lessons.summary: A token opens the door the role allows, in the division the pair names.

lessons.title: SCIM and other directory sync still start with an OAuth client
lessons.summary: The OAuth article points SCIM at a client. The client still has roles and a grant.

tracks.title: AppFoundry and CRM
tracks.summary: The marketplace, the documented Salesforce and Zendesk embeds, and OAuth migrations that do not invent other CRMs.

lessons.title: AppFoundry is the marketplace, not a feature you assume is installed
lessons.summary: An app is present only after someone installs it into the org.

lessons.title: Genesys Cloud for Salesforce is a documented embed
lessons.summary: Screen pop, click-to-dial, logging, and the assist features that page names.

lessons.title: Salesforce data actions move to OAuth client credentials
lessons.summary: Consumer key, secret, and My Domain URL. The request body of the action stays.

lessons.title: Zendesk has its own about page, with a similar embed idea
lessons.summary: Do not copy the Salesforce field list onto Zendesk.

lessons.title: Dynamics, ServiceNow, and the rest stay on the marketplace
lessons.summary: No invented feature lists for CRMs this lab did not open.

lessons.title: A CRM failure is not an ACD failure
lessons.summary: Screen pop can die while the queue is healthy.

tracks.title: Migration
tracks.summary: Engage, PureConnect, and Cisco UCCE move by rebuilding Architect flows and queues. This is a learning bridge, not a converter.

lessons.title: Nothing imports your old routing by magic
lessons.summary: You rebuild flows, queues, and trunks. You do not flip a converter this lab has not found.

lessons.title: Engage and PureConnect become flows and queues
lessons.summary: Strategies, IRDs, and handlers are read as behavior, then redrawn.

lessons.title: IVR becomes Architect tasks, menus, and audio
lessons.summary: CVP, UCCX prompts, and Engage voice all become the same kind of flow.

lessons.title: UCCE skill groups and precision queues are not Genesys queues
lessons.summary: Membership, skills, and bullseye are three ideas you reassemble.

lessons.title: UCCX is a smaller center with the same rebuild rule
lessons.summary: Scripts, CSQs, and the Finesse desktop do not move as files.

lessons.title: CUCM stays. BYOC is the door, not a replacement cluster.
lessons.summary: A dial plan and a trunk are Genesys number plans and a BYOC trunk. CUCM is still yours.

lessons.title: Webex is a neighbor, not a page this lab pretends to summarize
lessons.summary: Use Cisco’s product pages. Do not cite a Webex help URL this lab did not confirm.

lessons.title: Cut over one number, then the queue, then the people
lessons.summary: A weekend big-bang is how untested emergency routes meet a full staff.

tracks.title: Ecosystem
tracks.summary: How the tracks fit, how to read certifications, and what this lab refuses to invent.

lessons.title: The conversation crosses a short list of systems
lessons.summary: Carrier, trunk or Edge, Architect, queue, agent, then the systems beside the agent.

lessons.title: WFM, QM, E911, analytics, CRM, and bots are sisters
lessons.summary: Each sister has a track and a page. None of them is a setting on the queue tab alone.

lessons.title: The Cisco bridge is a translation, with both citations showing
lessons.summary: UCCE, UCCX, CUCM, and Webex are named so a Cisco engineer can find the door.

lessons.title: Read the catalog by name, then the announcement
lessons.summary: GC-GCP and GC-GCD are catalog codes. Specialist rows are names. AI rows are two exams.

lessons.title: Interview answers cite a page, not a vibe
lessons.summary: The drill in this lab is a set of questions with a model answer and a link.

lessons.title: What this lab will not invent
lessons.summary: Prices, unconfirmed hosts, exam codes, lifecycle dates, and CRM feature lists stay off the page.

studios.title: Architect-style flow builder
studios.summary: A vertical task list that exports learning JSON. It is not an import file for a live org.

studios.title: Routing simulator
studios.summary: Conversation score, bullseye rings, preferred agents, and evaluation methods as the articles describe them.

studios.title: Platform API explorer
studios.summary: Sample requests and JSON for grants and queues. The page never sends them.

studios.title: Number plan desk
studios.summary: Classify a dial string with the documented default plans. Not the in-product call simulator.

studios.title: Migration mapper
studios.summary: A learning bridge from Engage, PureConnect, and Cisco UCCE to objects you rebuild.
